stored_query: How do I enable audit delivery for service meridian in the test environment?
stored_answer: For service meridian in the test environment, first identify the test-only configuration bundle and confirm that it is not the production bundle. Open the service settings and enable audit delivery only for the test tenant. Set the audit destination to the test collector, not the production collector. Confirm that the destination is reachable and that the service account has write permission for that destination. Apply the configuration during a maintenance window and retain the previous configuration for rollback. Send one synthetic audit event and verify it appears in the test collector with the expected tenant tag and timestamp. Confirm that no event appears in the production collector. Record the configuration revision and the operator who approved the change. If any check fails, restore the previous bundle and investigate before retrying. This procedure is specific to meridian in the test environment. It does not authorize production changes, does not grant access to another tenant, does not change retention, does not disable audit logging, and does not prove that unrelated services are configured correctly. Review the emitted event carefully, because a successful settings response alone does not establish delivery. Keep the test collector address in server-side configuration, and never paste a credential into a request or a log. Recheck the destination after service restart. Repeat the synthetic event check after configuration deployment so that a stale process cannot silently use its earlier destination. Document the result and preserve the old revision until the rollback window closes.
